title: Kernel Concierge Mapper for Runtime Quant Switching
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Implement a runtime "kernel concierge" — a lightweight decision factory that maps incoming inference requests to the best execution path (FP16 / FP8 / INT8 kernels) based on per-model quant profiles, request shape, latency SLO, and accuracy guardrails. This ticket covers policy design, fast lookup/score computation, fail-safe fallback logic, and the rollout/validation pipeline.

Background: We already have profiling and offline quant calibration pipelines that produce per-layer FP8/INT8 profiles and a model-level quality delta estimate. Previously, kernel choice was static per-deployment. For cost and latency improvements we need a runtime mapper that can safely choose mixed-precision paths while preserving customer-facing quality and SLOs.

Constraints: must add <2ms median decision overhead, be horizontally scalable, cheaply cache decisions, provide deterministic reproducibility for A/B, and be auditable (trace the decision inputs and selected kernel). Any change must include shadow validation and automatic rollback triggers on quality regressions.
acceptance_criteria: Runtime decision path added to serving runtime with end-to-end latency overhead <2ms p50 for 99% of requests
Decision logic chooses a quant path consistent with per-model quant profile and the configured safety policy
Fallback to FP16 when safety checks fail or telemetry indicates degradation
Telemetry emits per-decision tags (model, profile_id, reason, chosen_path) and integrates with console dashboards
Shadow validation runs for canary rollout and detection rules can trigger automatic rollback or quarantine
design_notes: High-level design: 1) Decision factory uses a compact scoring function: score = w_quality*expected_quality_delta + w_latency*expected_latency_improvement + w_cost*expected_cost_saving - penalty_if_unvalidated. 2) Inputs: model_id, quant_profile_id, request_sequence_length, batch_size_hint, route_policy (latency/cost/throughput), recent telemetry fingerprints. 3) Store quant profile metadata (calibration confidence, per-layer scale stability, offline eval delta distribution) in a small key-value lookup with TTL. 4) For performance, precompute a small candidate set per-model (FP16, FP8-fast, FP8-safe, INT8-confident) and use a finite-state matching table to avoid per-request heavy computation. 5) Safety layers: shadow execution of selected quant path on a 1% sampling; golden-run compare using lightweight metrics (logprob delta, token-error-rate proxies). 6) Decision trace must be attached to request span and surfaced in console. 7) Runtime exposes hooks to force override and flags for experiments.
implementation_plan: Phase 1: Implement decision factory service interface + in-memory candidate cache and scoring defaults
Phase 2: Integrate per-model quant_profile metadata store and build profile ingestion from calibration pipeline
Phase 3: Add lightweight telemetry tags AND shadow-execution sampler to serving runtime
Phase 4: Implement safety policy engine (thresholds, quarantine rules, automatic fallback)
Phase 5: End-to-end tests, load validation, and canary rollout with monitoring alerts
validation_plan: Offline: Run candidate selection against historical traces and compute expected quality delta distribution and tail-latency impacts.
Shadow validation: 1% sample where quant path runs side-by-side with FP16 golden run; collect comparison vectors and produce daily drift reports.
Canary: 10% traffic for 48 hours with strict SLO/quality gates; if any gate trips auto-revert to FP16 for that model/version.
Gradual rollout: increase by 10% steps with health checks and automatic step-back on regression signals.
Continuous: compare live production embeddings/response-quality proxies against baseline using lightweight model-sensitivity tests
risks: Calibration confidence is noisy for rare sequence-length distributions leading to misrouting
Shadow sampling overhead may introduce measurable GPU cost if not throttled
Overly aggressive scoring weights may bias toward cost at quality expense
Decision trace volume could increase observability storage costs
telemetry_and_metrics: slo.latency and slo.error-rate - must not degrade beyond configured SLAs
cost.per-token delta by model and path
